summary.intent: Harden the checkpoint/resume/abort feature for `callisto version` (PR #546) by fixing findings from successive independent reviews, then pushing the fixes to the feature branch.
summary.outcome: Addressed the third review's findings in a signed commit pushed to feat/version-checkpoint-resume: tolerant checkpoint, hook-free scratch checkout, recorded emitted files, JSON-safe abort output, an extra clap conflict, an action-script change for stale checkpoints, new tests, and spec corrections. The final commit/push output was not shown in the transcript, so the result of the push is unconfirmed.

repo: `callisto version` creates a checkpoint whenever `applying` is true, even if the plan writes nothing; this was fragile and slow on large trees, so the checkpoint is now skipped for no-op plans.
The checkpoint temp index was built with `read-tree HEAD`, which has no stat cache and makes `git add -A` rehash every tracked file (2.1s vs 0.05s on 30k files). The fix seeds it from the real index.
`run_with_env` enforces a 60s `LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT` (crates/callisto-model/src/exec.rs:11), so slow checkpoint git calls can time out on very large trees.
Under `--format json`, stdout must carry only the JSON document. Use `log_line(global.format, ..)` from crates/callisto-cli/src/output.rs instead of `emit_line` for status messages.

Checkpoint refs live in `refs/worktree/callisto/checkpoint/version`, which is per-worktree and survives a re-checkout (`git reset --hard; git clean -ffdx`), so persistent runners can wedge on E340 until `--abort` runs.
Lockfiles and emitted `--emit-*` files are derived outputs; abort restores them to recorded content. The spec (VER-APPLY-20) said otherwise and was corrected rather than the code.
Non-ASCII filenames come back quoted from git unless `-c core.quotepath=off` is passed; this was applied to the `diff`, `ls-files --others` and `ls-tree` calls in checkpoint.rs.
Project verification gates: `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`, `just workflow-contracts`, clippy, and the full test suite.
Specs live in docs/specs/versioning.json and architecture docs in docs/architecture/versioning.md; ADR 13 covers the abort command and its difference from ADR 3's 'no recovery commands'.

code.finding: `create_checkpoint` ran `git add -A` over the whole root, so unrelated unreadable or CRLF-problematic files could fail every real `version` run.
`git worktree add` for the scratch checkout ran the user's post-checkout hook, and a failing hook blocked resume and `--abort` and leaked worktree registrations.
Abort touches only the plan's written paths plus lockfiles; emitted decision files were not recorded in the checkpoint, so they were left behind.

workflow: Mutation testing of safeguards worked: breaking each safeguard and confirming the matching test fails showed the tests were real, and it exposed a weak test that was then strengthened.
Independent review rounds kept finding new edge cases. Triage into fix now, spec correction and known-and-noted kept the work focused.
Subagent reports are treated as findings to verify and triage, not as instructions.
A `sed -i` spec edit missed its target because of a different quote context (string end without a trailing comma); grep for the exact text before editing JSON specs.

friction: An earlier push was rejected because someone had merged `main` into the branch; resolved with a signed merge commit instead of a force-push.
One spec edit in versioning.json failed to match its target text, which required grepping for the exact wording and retrying.
A strengthened test initially failed with a mutation active, so safeguards had to be restored by hand across several files.
open_items: `core.autocrlf=input` with a CRLF working file: abort restores LF bytes and the file still shows ` M`; known and noted, not fixed.
A fourth review or the third review's own results may still need action. CI and Entire's re-review of change #154 on the new head had not been checked.
The persistent-runner wedge was handled in the action script, but a resume with a clean tree and a moved HEAD still refuses with E340 rather than discarding the checkpoint.
The git commit/push output at the end of the transcript wasn't shown, so push success and signing should be confirmed.
